title: Comprehensive Mono Process Textbook Structural Audit

findings.title: Legacy RT-core notation persists alongside the canonical RT-core form
findings.impact: The textbook presents two active-looking RT-core forms: the legacy delta_a/iff_R form and the updated canonical RT_core form. The later canonical block exists, but the earlier form is not marked as historical residue, so a reader can treat both as current authority.
findings.suggested_correction: Mark the legacy form as historical residue or replace it everywhere with the canonical RT_core form. Keep only one current canonical expression in the textbook body.
findings.governance_patch_recommendation: Add a textbook-sync patch that normalizes chapter 1 and chapter 1.2D to the canonical RT_core spelling and explicitly labels any retained legacy notation as backward-compatibility aliasing.

findings.title: Section 6.4 closes before the crisis fork is fully formalized
findings.impact: The section introduces the empty-set failure case and two branches, but it does not supply the full crisis branch, recovery branch, state-transition equations, convergence proof, or return condition that the heading advertises.
findings.suggested_correction: Expand 6.4 with the formal crisis branch, empty admissibility resolution, orientation reselection, recursive continuation, explicit transition equations, proof of convergence, failure branch, recovery branch, and return-to-stable-regime condition.
findings.governance_patch_recommendation: Create a textbook refactor patch for section 6.4 and bind it to the admissibility kernel governance chain.

findings.title: Chapter 13 contains a malformed trace chain ending in an undefined \to_x token
findings.impact: The displayed relation chain `(*|*) -> (A|E) -> <*>_x -> ->_x` ends with an undefined transition token. The same `x` is explicitly reserved as a discussion placeholder elsewhere, so the equation reads as truncated or malformed rather than complete.
findings.suggested_correction: Replace the dangling \to_x fragment with a defined operator or a complete domain label, and ensure the chain terminates with an actual target expression.
findings.governance_patch_recommendation: Add a notation repair patch for the economics projection block and mirror the fix into any paired SSOT artifact.

findings.title: Appendix G points to non-existent docs/registry targets
findings.impact: The three registry links in the secondary references section use a docs/registry root that does not exist in the repository.
findings.suggested_correction: Retarget the links to registry/compliance_charter_v2_3.json, registry/operator_registry.json, and registry/lexicon_canonical.json.
findings.governance_patch_recommendation: Add a documentation sync patch for Appendix G registry links.

findings.title: Appendix G links a missing results artifact
findings.impact: The CLS_003 reference points to results/2026-06-16_run03_CLS_003_EXTREME/paper.md, but the result folder and paper are absent from the repository.
findings.suggested_correction: Restore the missing result artifact, or retarget the citation to the actual archived paper if the run was moved or renamed.
findings.governance_patch_recommendation: Create a result-archive repair note or update the citation matrix.

findings.title: Five open memory-tensor lexicon terms are not surfaced as explicit textbook entries
findings.impact: The queue still carries memory_tensor_array, implied_memory, conditioned_memory_frame, memory_slice_trajectory, and gradient_based_memory_inference as GAP_OPEN items, but the textbook only mentions the memory-tensor program at a high level.
findings.suggested_correction: Add explicit Appendix F entries or chapter notes for the five memory-tensor terms, or mark them as intentionally deferred TODOs in the textbook itself.
findings.governance_patch_recommendation: Add a memory-tensor lexicon sync patch or annotate the terms as deferred in Appendix F.

notes: All explicit file:/// links in the textbook resolved successfully.
All inline path-like [Source: ...] citations that look like local files resolved successfully.
Appendix F contains many deliberate open items; those are tracked rather than silently omitted.
